market_holds: Spot $4.005 at the 2026-11-18 close (sealed baseline). There is no option market, so no implied move. My own read of Yahoo daily bars gives past close-to-close reactions on print days of about +10% (Nov 2024), +9.4% (Mar 2025), +1.0% (Nov 2025, after a +9% gap), -10.1% (Mar 2026), +11.6% (May 2026) and -11.1% (Aug 2026), so the usual move is about 10% with no consistent sign. Run-in is -4.4% over 5 days and +1.4% over 20 days. Over the same spans KWEB did -7.8% and -8.1%, JD -10.1% and -2.9%, and BABA -15.7% and -18.0%. So RERE held up against a falling China-internet tape, and its last week tracks that tape rather than any news of its own. On the company's own Q3 guide of RMB6.34-6.44B (+23.1-25.1%, issued 2026-08-20), the stock fell 11% on 2026-08-20 although the Q2 beat was large. FY2026 consensus revenue is RMB26.8B (range 26.2-27.0B, stockanalysis/S&P, age unknown). That implies Q4 of about RMB7.38-7.64B, or +18-22% on the Q4'25 base of RMB6,254M, depending on whether Q3 lands at the guide midpoint or at the company's usual beat. Price targets average $6.64 and all four analysts rate it Strong Buy; the latest action was UBS initiating at $5.50 on 2026-07-21. Short interest is unknown.
view: The stock trades on the next-quarter revenue guide, not the quarter. Each recent print beat the top of its own guide: Q4'25 by 1.2%, Q1'26 by 3.4% and Q2'26 by 4.2%. So a Q3 of roughly RMB6.6-6.7B (+27-30%) against a 6.44B top end is the base case, and the market expects it. The reaction then rests on the Q4 guide's growth rate against the deceleration path. The guided growth rate went from about 25-27% (Q4'25) to 26-28% (Q1'26), 25-27% (Q2'26) and 23-25% (Q3'26). The flat guides drew +11.6% in May and -10% in March, the March drop coming after an +11.7% run-up the day before. The step down drew -11% in August. Pulling the Q4 guide down are a tough comp (Q4'25 was +29% on a strong iPhone 17 cycle and trade-in subsidies), Chinese new-phone shipments falling 10-15% YoY in Q3 with Counterpoint expecting more pressure in Q4, and a 2026 subsidy pool fully handed out by end-September. Holding it up are used-phone ASPs up 8-10% YTD at Zhuanzhuan, Zhuanzhuan recycle orders +37% YTD with October the year's high, iPhone 18 Pro China sales +23.5% at launch at a price 1,000 yuan higher, which pushes buyers toward used phones, and 1P gross margin of 15.7% against 13.2% a year earlier. My central guess is a conservative Q4 guide of about +19-23%, i.e. RMB7.45-7.70B. That is roughly where FY consensus already sits, so I cannot place the line on one side of what the price holds. There may be a slight downward lean from another step down in guided growth, which this stock has punished, offset by a cheap multiple and strong margin and industry data. No call.

recommendation.reason: The deciding line is the Q4 revenue guide's growth rate. The company guides conservatively, and FY consensus of about RMB26.8B already implies Q4 growth of +18-22%, which is about where a typical conservative guide would land. Industry data since the last call point both ways: used-phone prices and recycling volumes are strong, new-phone shipments and subsidies are weaker. Nothing dated shows the price is behind on either side.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 guide at or above +25% YoY (RMB7.8B or more), or a Q3 beat above RMB6.8B with 1P margin expanding again, would make up the more likely side. A guide below +18% (under RMB7.38B) would confirm the downside.

self_critique: The upside case is stronger than my number shows. The stock is about 10x earnings, has outperformed a collapsing China-internet tape by about 9pp over 20 days, and has beaten the top of its guide by a widening margin through 2026. Memory-driven inflation in new-phone prices structurally favours used-phone sellers, and a Q4 guide of +23% or more plus a big Q3 beat could rerun the May +11.6%. The downside case: the guide has stepped down every recent quarter, Q4 faces its toughest comp, and the China tape is weak into the open. Neither side has dated evidence that the price is behind.
